mainTopic: Midrashic readings of names and verses about מרדכי and אסתר, including why מרדכי is called יהודי and the side discussion of בתיה בת פרעה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבא's reading of 'what the יהודי did to me and what the ימיני paid me back.' דוד spared שמעי, ancestor of מרדכי, and שאול spared אגג, ancestor of המן. רבי יוחנן says מרדכי was really from בנימין and is called יהודי because he rejected עבודה זרה. רבי שמעון בן פזי then shows the same idea in דברי הימים: בתיה בת פרעה is called היהודיה for rejecting her father's idols. From the same פסוק the גמרא learns that raising an orphan counts as giving birth, and that all six names in it are nicknames for משה. It also explains why כלב is called מרד. The גמרא then goes back to מגילת אסתר and explains verse after verse: מרדכי going into exile on his own, the names הדסה and אסתר, her being an orphan, and רבי מאיר's reading that מרדכי married her. It goes on through her seven maids, her food, the oil of myrrh, and how she found favor with everyone. It ends with the king's failed attempts to make her reveal her people, and רבי אלעזר begins a new teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two kings who did not kill their enemies
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes explaining the complaint of כנסת ישראל. The יהודי, meaning דוד, did not kill שמעי, so מרדכי was born and המן grew jealous of him. The ימיני, meaning שאול, did not kill אגג, so המן was born and caused Israel suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: That דוד did not kill שמעי, and from him מרדכי was born, the man המן was jealous of. And "what the Benjamite paid me back" means that שאול did not kill אגג, and from him המן was born, who made Israel suffer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of רבא's explanation of a complaint by the Jewish people: "See what the יהודי did to me and what the ימיני paid me back." Here רבא explains both halves of that complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, "יהודי" points to דוד from שבט יהודה, and "ימיני" points to שאול from שבט בנימין. Each king spared someone he should have killed. Sparing שמעי led to מרדכי, whom המן hated, and sparing אגג led to המן himself. Together these two mistakes set up the danger of the פורים story.

keyTerms.meaning: Shimei ben Gera, the man from בנימין who cursed דוד; an ancestor of מרדכי
a Benjamite, someone from שבט בנימין
the king of עמלק whom שאול spared

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of רבא's statement. The phrase "what the יהודי did to me" was said just before this, and our first line explains it.

phrases.english: that David did not kill Shimei,
so that Mordechai was born from him,
the one Haman was jealous of.
And "what the Benjamite paid me back" means:
that Saul did not kill Agag,
so that Haman was born from him,
who made Israel suffer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement on the previous amud, explaining both halves of the phrase "מה עשה לי יהודי ומה שילם לי ימיני."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "יהודי" refers to דוד, who spared שמעי, ancestor of מרדכי. "ימיני" refers to שאול, who spared אגג, ancestor of המן.

steps.title: מרדכי was from בנימין, called יהודי for rejecting idols
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says מרדכי really came from בנימין. He is called "יהודי" because he rejected עבודה זרה, and anyone who rejects עבודה זרה is called "יהודי". The proof is a פסוק in דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Really, מרדכי came from בנימין. So why is he called "יהודי"? Because he rejected עבודה זרה. Anyone who rejects עבודה זרה is called "יהודי", as it says: "There are certain Jewish men..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new answer to the question of how מרדכי can be both "איש יהודי" and "איש ימיני". In his view, "יהודי" is not about his tribe at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers tried to connect מרדכי to שבט יהודה in some way. רבי יוחנן says his tribe was simply בנימין. "יהודי" is a title for anyone who rejects idols. His proof is the פסוק about חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, called "יהודאין" because they refused to bow to the idol.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually; introduces the speaker's true position
here: someone who rejects idols, not only a member of שבט יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, anyone who rejects עבודה זרה earns the name "יהודי".
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea gives the name "יהודי" a meaning based on faith, not only on tribe. The rest of this passage builds on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Really, he came from Binyamin,
phrases.notes: "He" is מרדכי. רבי יוחנן says his tribe was simply בנימין, with no family tie to יהודה.

phrases.english: so why is he called "Yehudi"?
Because he rejected idol worship.
For anyone who rejects idol worship is called "Yehudi,"
as it is written: "There are certain Jewish men, etc."
phrases.notes: This is from ספר דניאל, about חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם מִבִּנְיָמִן קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from the earlier views, including רבא's, which tied "יהודי" to שבט יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרדכי was from בנימין. He is called "יהודי" because anyone who rejects עבודה זרה is called "יהודי".

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן פזי's opening to דברי הימים
steps.stepSummary: Whenever רבי שמעון בן פזי began teaching דברי הימים, he said that all its words are one and we know how to explain them. Then he quoted a פסוק that calls a woman "היהודיה" and later names her בתיה בת פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי שמעון בן פזי opened his teaching of דברי הימים, he said: All your words are one, and we know how to explain them. "And his wife, the יהודיה, gave birth to ירד father of גדור, חבר father of שוכו, and יקותיאל father of זנוח, and these are the sons of בתיה בת פרעה, whom מרד married."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching because it also uses the word "יהודי". This step is setup: it quotes the פסוק, and the next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "All your words are one" means דברי הימים often calls the same person by different names, and we must explain each name. In this פסוק, the woman called "היהודיה" turns out to be בתיה בת פרעה, an Egyptian princess. That creates the puzzle the גמרא is about to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: to explain them by דרש, finding the deeper meaning
Bisya, daughter of Pharaoh, who married מרד

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
when he would open his teaching of Divrei HaYamim,
said this:
All your words are one,
phrases.notes: He is talking to the ספר itself. Many names in it can point to one and the same person.

phrases.english: and we know how to explain them.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִשְׁתּוֹ הַיְהוּדִיָּה יָלְדָה אֶת יֶרֶד אֲבִי גְדוֹר
phrases.english: "And his wife, the Yehudiya, gave birth to Yered the father of Gedor,
and Chever the father of Socho,
and Yekusiel the father of Zanoach,
and these are the sons of Bisya the daughter of Pharaoh,
whom Mered married."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי, כִּי הֲוָה פָּתַח בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought because it is connected to רבי יוחנן's idea that "יהודי" means someone who rejects עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דברי הימים must be explained by דרש. One example is a פסוק where the woman called "היהודיה" is בתיה בת פרעה.

steps.title: Why is פרעה's daughter called יהודיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בתיה, an Egyptian princess, is called "יהודיה".
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is she called "יהודיה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the obvious question raised by the פסוק and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בתיה was the daughter of פרעה, not a member of שבט יהודה. Calling her "יהודיה" needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: a Jewish woman; the female form of יהודי

phrases.english: Why is she called "Yehudiya"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the word "היהודיה" in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a daughter of פרעה would be called "יהודיה".

steps.title: She rejected her father's idols
steps.stepSummary: She is called "יהודיה" because she rejected עבודה זרה. The proof is the פסוק "ותרד בת פרעה לרחוץ על היאור", which רבי יוחנן explains as washing herself clean of her father's idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she rejected עבודה זרה, as it says: "And Pharaoh's daughter went down to wash at the river." And רבי יוחנן said: she went down to wash herself clean of the idols of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question using רבי יוחנן's rule from step 2: anyone who rejects עבודה זרה is called "יהודי". It proves that בתיה rejected idols from the story of her going down to the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken simply, "going down to wash" sounds like a plain bath. רבי יוחנן reads it as a spiritual washing: she was cleaning herself of her father's idol worship. That is what earns her the name "יהודיה", the same way מרדכי earned the name "יהודי".

keyTerms.meaning: idols (a word showing contempt for them)

steps.whatToRemember: Both מרדכי and בתיה בת פרעה are called "יהודי" or "יהודיה" because they rejected עבודה זרה, not because of which tribe they came from.

phrases.english: Because she rejected idol worship,
as it is written: "And the daughter of Pharaoh went down
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות where she goes down to the river and finds baby משה.

phrases.english: to wash at the river,"
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
that she went down to wash
from the idols of her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 using the rule from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בתיה is called "יהודיה" because she rejected her father's idols. This is learned from "ותרד בת פרעה לרחוץ על היאור" as רבי יוחנן explains it.

steps.title: Did בתיה really give birth to משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'ילדה' (she gave birth), because בתיה only raised משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says she 'gave birth'? But she only raised him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a problem in the פסוק: it says היהודיה 'gave birth' to ירד, who is משה, but בתיה did not give birth to משה. She only raised him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already assumes that every name in this פסוק is משה. The full explanation comes in step 8. Since everyone knows יוכבד gave birth to משה, the word 'ילדה' cannot be meant literally. So the גמרא pushes back on the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: "Gave birth"? But she only raised him!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק from step 3: 'his wife היהודיה gave birth to ירד...' The גמרא treats ירד as משה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying היהודיה as בתיה, the גמרא now questions the next word of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בתיה did not physically give birth to משה. She only raised him, so 'gave birth' looks inaccurate.

steps.title: Raising an orphan counts as giving birth
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'gave birth' on purpose: whoever raises an orphan is treated as the child's parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that anyone who raises an orphan boy or girl in his home is credited by the פסוק as if he gave birth to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק chose the word 'gave birth' on purpose. It teaches that raising an orphan is like giving birth to that child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word is not a mistake. It carries a lesson. בתיה raised משה, so the פסוק calls her his mother. From her case we learn a general rule about anyone who raises an orphan.

keyTerms.meaning: to tell you, to teach you a lesson
the פסוק credits him, treats him as

steps.whatToRemember: Whoever raises an orphan in his home is treated by the פסוק as if he gave birth to that child.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous lesson about how much raising an orphan is worth, and it is learned from בתיה and משה.

phrases.english: To tell you that anyone who raises
an orphan boy or orphan girl in his home —
the verse credits him as if he gave birth to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לְךָ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְגַדֵּל יָתוֹם וִיתוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on the word 'ילדה'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The odd wording is intentional and teaches a lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ילדה' looked inaccurate, since בתיה only raised משה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Raising an orphan counts as giving birth, so the פסוק calls בתיה his mother.

steps.title: Every name in the פסוק is a nickname for משה
steps.stepSummary: The names ירד, גדור, חבר, סוכו, יקותיאל and זנוח all refer to משה. Each one describes something he did for Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירד is משה. Why is he called ירד? Because the מן came down for Israel in his days. גדור, because he fenced up Israel's breaches. חבר, because he connected Israel to their Father in Heaven. סוכו, because he was like a shelter for Israel. יקותיאל, because Israel hoped to God in his days. זנוח, because he made Israel's sins be put aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the different names in the פסוק are not different people. They are six nicknames for משה, and each one is based on a word that sounds like the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why step 6 could assume that ירד is משה. Each name is linked to a similar-sounding Hebrew word: ירד goes with ירד (came down), גדור with גדר (fence), חבר with חיבר (connected), סוכו with סוכה (shelter), יקותיאל with קוו לאל (hoped to God), and זנוח with הזניח (put aside). So the whole פסוק becomes a list of משה's greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: the heavenly bread that fell in the desert
he set aside, caused to be ignored

steps.confusionAlert: These are not six different children of בתיה. The גמרא reads all six names as one person, משה.

phrases.english: "Jered" — this is Moses,
and why was he called "Jered"?
Because the manna came down for Israel in his days.
"Gedor" — because he fenced up the breaches of Israel.
"Heber" — because he connected Israel
to their Father in Heaven.
"Soco" — because he became like a shelter for Israel.
"Jekuthiel" — because Israel hoped to God in his days.
"Zanoah" — because he caused Israel's sins to be set aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק and explains the assumption from step 6 that ירד is משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All six names in the פסוק are nicknames of משה, each describing one of his good deeds for Israel.

steps.title: The three times 'אבי' means משה was a father in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אבי' appears three times in the פסוק, showing that משה was a father in תורה, in wisdom and in נבואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Father of', 'father of', 'father of': a father in תורה, a father in wisdom, a father in prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the פסוק says 'אבי' (father of) three times. It explains that this shows three ways משה was a father to Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'אבי' shows up between the names: 'ירד אבי גדור, חבר אבי סוכו, יקותיאל אבי זנוח'. Since all the names are משה, 'father' cannot mean a real father of a son. It describes משה as the leading teacher of Israel in three areas.

phrases.english: "Father of," "father of," "father of" —
phrases.notes: These are the three times 'אבי' appears in the same פסוק: ירד אבי גדור, חבר אבי סוכו, יקותיאל אבי זנוח.

phrases.aramaic: אָב בַּתּוֹרָה, אָב בְּחׇכְמָה, אָב בִּנְבִיאוּת.
phrases.english: a father in Torah, a father in wisdom, a father in prophecy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the names, the גמרא explains the repeated word 'אבי' in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was a father to Israel in תורה, in wisdom and in נבואה.

steps.title: Why is בתיה's husband called מרד?
steps.stepSummary: The end of the same פסוק says בתיה was taken by מרד, but her husband was כלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And these are the sons of בתיה, whom מרד took.' Was his name מרד? Wasn't his name כלב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the same פסוק from step 3, which says בתיה married someone named מרד. It asks how that can be, since her husband was כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא takes it as known that בתיה married כלב. So the name 'מרד' looks wrong. This sets up the answer that 'מרד' is a description, not a real name.

keyTerms.meaning: rebellion; here the name of her husband in the פסוק
כלב בן יפנה, one of the two good spies

phrases.english: "And these are the sons of Bithiah whom Mered took,"
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק in דברי הימים, where בתיה is named as בת פרעה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֶרֶד שְׁמוֹ? וַהֲלֹא כָּלֵב שְׁמוֹ!
phrases.english: Was his name Mered? Wasn't his name Caleb?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֶרֶד שְׁמוֹ? וַהֲלֹא כָּלֵב שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another hard word in the same פסוק about בתיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The husband's name 'מרד' in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בתיה's husband was כלב, so calling him מרד seems wrong.

steps.title: Two rebels married each other
steps.stepSummary: כלב is called מרד because he rebelled against the spies' plan, and he married בתיה, who rebelled against her father's idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Let כלב, who rebelled against the plan of the spies, come and marry the daughter of פרעה, who rebelled against the idols of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'מרד' is a nickname for כלב, meaning 'the rebel'. It explains that הקדוש ברוך הוא matched him with בתיה because both of them rebelled for the good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב refused to go along with the bad report of the מרגלים. בתיה turned away from her father's idols, as we saw in step 5. The name 'מרד' shows why the two were a fitting match.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: בתיה rejected her father's idols, which is why she is called 'יהודיה'. She raised משה, so she is counted as his mother. She married כלב, a fellow 'rebel' for the good.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let Caleb, who rebelled against the plan of the spies, come
and marry the daughter of Pharaoh
who rebelled against the idols of her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יָבֹא כָּלֵב שֶׁמָּרַד בַּעֲצַת מְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why כלב is called מרד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The name is a description (nickname), not a real name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מרד' looked like the wrong name for בתיה's husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מרד' describes כלב as the one who rebelled against the spies, a fitting match for בתיה, who rebelled against idols.

steps.title: מרדכי went into exile on his own
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק 'who had been exiled from Jerusalem' as teaching that מרדכי left ירושלים by his own choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about מרדכי, 'who had been exiled from Jerusalem.' רבא said: this means he went into exile on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to explaining the פסוקים about מרדכי. רבא teaches that מרדכי chose to go into גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק sounds like מרדכי was forced out with everyone else. רבא reads it as describing מרדכי's own choice to leave, not something that only happened to him. This is a new point about the פסוק and does not answer any question.

keyTerms.meaning: was exiled, was sent into exile

phrases.english: "Who had been exiled from Jerusalem"
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק in מגילת אסתר describing מרדכי.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That he went into exile on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of the Divrei HaYamim names (steps 8-11), the גמרא goes back to the next phrase in the מגילה about מרדכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרדכי went into exile voluntarily.

steps.title: Why does the queen have two names?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls her הדסה and also אסתר. The גמרא asks which is her real name.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And he raised הדסה.' It calls her הדסה, and it also calls her אסתר. Why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that one person has two names and asks about it. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says 'הדסה, she is אסתר.' The גמרא wants to know which name is her real one and where the other name comes from. The answer comes in the following steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Hadassah; also the word for a myrtle

phrases.english: "And he had brought up Hadassah"
It calls her "Hadassah"
And it calls her "Esther"?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי לַהּ הֲדַסָּה וְקָרֵי לַהּ אֶסְתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מרדכי to the next phrase in the פסוק, which is about אסתר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which name, הדסה or אסתר, was her real name, and why was she also given the other one?

steps.title: רבי מאיר: her name was אסתר, and הדסה describes her righteousness
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says her real name was אסתר. She was called הדסה because צדיקים are compared to myrtles.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says her name was אסתר. Why was she called הדסה? Because צדיקים are called myrtles, as the פסוק says, 'And he stood among the myrtles.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The first opinion, רבי מאיר, says אסתר was her real name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, 'הדסה' is not a name but a title of praise. Since צדיקים are called myrtles in a פסוק in זכריה, calling her הדסה means she was a צדקת.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
Esther was her name,
And why was she called Hadassah?
Because of the righteous,
Who are called myrtles.
And so it says:
"And he stood among the myrtles."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from זכריה, and the 'myrtles' there are read as the צדיקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֶסְתֵּר שְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her real name was אסתר. הדסה is a title meaning 'righteous one,' based on the פסוק in זכריה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: her name was הדסה, and אסתר means she hid things
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says her real name was הדסה. She was called אסתר because she kept her background hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says her name was הדסה. Why was she called אסתר? Because she hid her matters, as the פסוק says, 'Esther did not tell her people.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא argues with רבי מאיר and flips it around: הדסה was the real name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה connects the name אסתר to the Hebrew root for 'hiding' (ס־ת־ר). Since she kept her people and family secret, she was called אסתר, 'the one who hides.'

keyTerms.meaning: her matters, the facts about her

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Hadassah was her name,
And why was she called Esther?
Because she would hide her matters,
phrases.notes: אסתר and מסתרת share the same letters. That is the wordplay.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"Esther did not tell her people, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about which name was the real one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her real name was הדסה. אסתר comes from 'hiding,' because she concealed her identity.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: אסתר was the name the nations gave her
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה agrees that her real name was הדסה. He says אסתר was what the non-Jews called her, after 'Istahar.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says her name was הדסה. Why was she called אסתר? Because the nations of the world called her after Istahar.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion agrees with רבי יהודה that הדסה was her real name. It gives a different reason for the name אסתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, אסתר is not a Hebrew wordplay at all. It is the foreign name the other nations used for her, taken from the word 'Istahar.'

keyTerms.meaning: Istahar, a bright light in the sky

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: Hadassah was her name,
And why was she called Esther?
Because the nations of the world would call her
After Istahar.
phrases.notes: Istahar is a foreign word for a bright, shining light in the sky. They named her after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with רבי יהודה that the real name was הדסה, but explains the name אסתר differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her real name was הדסה. אסתר was the non-Jewish name, from 'Istahar.'

steps.title: בן עזאי: הדסה describes her medium height
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי says she was called הדסה because she was medium height, like a myrtle.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: אסתר was not tall and not short, but medium, like a myrtle.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי gives another reason why she was called הדסה. This time the reason is about how she looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי explains where the name הדסה comes from, but unlike רבי מאיר's 'righteous' reason, his reason is physical: a myrtle is a medium-sized plant, and so was she.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: Esther
Was neither tall nor short,
But medium, like a myrtle.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: אֶסְתֵּר לֹא אֲרוּכָּה וְלֹא קְצָרָה הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another explanation of the name הדסה, different from רבי מאיר's 'righteous' reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She was called הדסה because she was medium height, like a myrtle.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: הדסה describes her greenish color
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says she was greenish, like a myrtle, but a thread of חסד made her beautiful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: אסתר was greenish, and a thread of grace was drawn over her.
steps.whatsHappening: The last opinion gives one more reason for the name הדסה. It is based on her coloring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A myrtle is green, and so her pale, greenish skin matched the name הדסה. Even so, a 'thread of חסד' rested on her, so people saw her as charming and beautiful.

keyTerms.meaning: a thread of grace or charm

steps.whatToRemember: There are two names, אסתר and הדסה. רבי מאיר says her name was אסתר and הדסה is praise for her righteousness. רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה say her name was הדסה, with אסתר meaning 'hiding' or coming from the nations' 'Istahar.' בן עזאי and רבי יהושע בן קרחה explain הדסה by her height or her color.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
Esther was greenish,
And a thread of grace was drawn over her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אָמַר: אֶסְתֵּר יְרַקְרוֹקֶת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final physical explanation of הדסה, alongside בן עזאי's height explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She was called הדסה because she was greenish like a myrtle, yet a thread of חסד made her beautiful.

steps.title: Why does the verse repeat that she had no parents?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק already said אסתר had no father or mother, so why does it then add 'when her father and mother died'?
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'For she had neither father nor mother.' So why do I need the next words, 'And when her father and mother were dead'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the same פסוק says the same fact twice and asks what the extra words come to teach. This sets up רב אחא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase already tells us she was an orphan. Since the פסוק does not waste words, the second phrase must be adding something new. The question is only about why the words are there; it does not argue with the fact itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Used when a phrase looks extra

phrases.english: "For she had neither father nor mother" —
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר chapter 2, the same פסוק that told us her names in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: "And when her father and mother were dead" — why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of her names (הדסה and אסתר) to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly extra phrase about her parents dying adds.

steps.title: She never had parents even for a single day
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא explains that her father died while her mother was pregnant with her, and her mother died when she was born.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said: When her mother became pregnant with her, her father died. When her mother gave birth to her, her mother died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers the question by explaining what the extra words teach about how she became an orphan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase tells us she was an orphan. The extra phrase tells us when it happened: her father died before she was born, and her mother died at her birth. So she never had a living father or mother, not even for one day.

keyTerms.meaning: She (her mother) became pregnant with her
She (her mother) gave birth to her

phrases.english: Rav Acha said:
When her mother became pregnant with her — her father died;
when her mother gave birth to her — her mother died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words teach the timing: her father died during the pregnancy and her mother died at the birth, so she never had parents at all.

steps.title: Read it as 'for a house,' meaning a wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר says to read 'לבת' (as a daughter) as 'לבית' (as a house), meaning מרדכי took אסתר as his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And when her father and mother died, מרדכי took her for himself as a daughter.' It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: Do not read it 'as a daughter' but rather 'as a house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that rereads one word of the פסוק, so it means מרדכי married אסתר instead of adopting her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לבת' and 'לבית' look and sound very much alike. In the language of חז"ל, a 'house' often means a man's wife. So רבי מאיר teaches that מרדכי took אסתר as his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as ... but rather as ...; a way of rereading a word to learn a lesson
As a house, meaning as a wife

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not erase the plain meaning of the פסוק. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of it.

phrases.english: "And when her father and mother were dead,
Mordechai took her for himself as a daughter."
It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Do not read "as a daughter," but rather "as a house."
phrases.notes: A 'house' here means a wife, so the point is that מרדכי married her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר אַל תִּקְרֵי לְבַת אֶלָּא לְבַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next words of the same פסוק and opens a new idea about how she was related to מרדכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read 'לבת' as 'לבית': מרדכי took אסתר as his wife.

steps.title: Support from the poor man's lamb
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings support from נתן's parable of the poor man's lamb, which also uses the word 'כבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the פסוק says: 'But the poor man had nothing except one little lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him and his children. It ate from his bread, drank from his cup, lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes another פסוק that uses the same word 'כבת' to back up רבי מאיר's reading. The next step will explain how this פסוק proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parable is about a man who took another man's wife. Its last words, 'like a daughter to him,' are the key, because the same word 'בת' shows up in a context that is clearly about a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says; brings a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: And so it says:
"But the poor man had nothing
phrases.notes: This is the parable נתן הנביא told דוד המלך after the story of בת שבע (שמואל ב, chapter 12).

phrases.english: except one little ewe lamb
which he had bought and raised;
and it grew up together with him and with his children;
it ate from his bread and drank from his cup,
and lay in his bosom,
and was like a daughter to him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a supporting פסוק for רבי מאיר's rereading in step 21.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נתן's parable of the poor man's lamb, which ends with 'ותהי לו כבת.'

steps.title: Why 'like a daughter' must mean a wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that 'כבת' in the parable cannot mean a daughter, because it lay in his bosom. It must mean a wife, and the same is true for אסתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because it lay in his bosom, it was like a daughter to him? Rather, it means it was like a wife to him. So too here, with אסתר, it means 'as a wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that is not really a question, to show that the simple reading 'like a daughter' does not fit the parable. Then it uses this to finish the proof for אסתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying in someone's bosom describes a wife, not a daughter. So in the parable, 'כבת' must mean like a wife. Since the same word means 'wife' there, it can mean 'wife' with אסתר too.

keyTerms.meaning: So too here; applies the conclusion to our case

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, מרדכי married אסתר. He reads 'לבת' as 'לבית' and proves it from the parable of the lamb, where 'כבת' clearly means a wife.

phrases.english: Because it lay in his bosom,
it was to him (as a daughter)?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question: lying in his bosom does not describe a daughter.

phrases.english: Rather — (as a house, meaning a wife).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, לְבַיִת. Either way, 'house' here means a wife.

phrases.english: So too here, "as a house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 22 proves the reading in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That 'לבת' with אסתר means 'as a wife.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: In the lamb parable, 'lay in his bosom' shows 'כבת' means a wife.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מרדכי took אסתר as a wife.

steps.title: The seven maids helped her keep track of the days
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that אסתר used her seven maids to count the days of the week, so she always knew when it was שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the seven maids, etc.' רבא said: She counted the days of the week by them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next פסוק, and רבא explains why the פסוק mentions that she had exactly seven maids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were seven maids for seven days, so each day had its own maid. By seeing which maid was serving her, אסתר could tell what day it was. That way she always knew when שבת came, even living in the palace.

phrases.english: "And the seven maids, etc."
phrases.notes: These were the maids given to her from the king's house (אסתר 2:9).

phrases.english: Rava said:
That she would count the days of the week by them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new פסוק and a new topic: אסתר's life in the palace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seven maids let her count the days of the week, so she kept track of שבת.

steps.title: הגי gave her Jewish food
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'he changed her' means הגי, the keeper of the women, gave אסתר Jewish food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he changed her and her maids, etc.' רב said: He fed her Jewish food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק, and רב says what the 'change' was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says הגי, who was in charge of the women, treated her differently from the others. רב says this means she got Jewish, כשר food, so she did not have to eat forbidden food in the palace.

keyTerms.meaning: And he changed her (moved her to better treatment)

phrases.english: "And he changed her and her maids, etc."
Rav said:
That he fed her Jewish food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next words of the פסוק and gives the first of three opinions. שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'He changed her' means she was given כשר food.

steps.title: הגי fed her pig meat
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says 'he changed her' means הגי fed her pig hinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: He fed her pig hinds.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different explanation of the same words, which argues with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל both agree הגי did something special for her through her food. רב says it was כשר food. שמואל says it was pig meat, which הגי probably meant as a fancy treat, even though it was not כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The back parts or hinds (of an animal)

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל argue about 'וישנה': רב says she got Jewish food, and שמואל says she was fed pig hinds.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
That he fed her pig hinds.
phrases.notes: He means הגי gave her this as special food, even though it is not כשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an explanation of 'וישנה' that argues with רב's in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'He changed her' means הגי fed her pig hinds.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: הגי fed her vegetables
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a third explanation of 'he changed her': הגי gave אסתר vegetables, and he proves this from דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: he gave her vegetables. The same thing is found with דניאל: 'So the steward took away their food and gave them vegetables.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a third opinion to the argument between רב and שמואל about what 'he changed her' means. He brings a פסוק from ספר דניאל to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said Jewish food, and שמואל said pig. רבי יוחנן takes a middle path: vegetables, which avoid any כשרות problem. His proof is that דניאל and his friends were also given vegetables in a non-Jewish palace so they would not eat forbidden food.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says. This introduces a פסוק as support.
Steward or guard in charge of food

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: vegetables.
And so it says:
"So the steward took away their royal food
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ספר דניאל, about דניאל and his friends in the king of Babylon's palace.

phrases.english: and gave them vegetables."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the רב and שמואל disagreement about 'he changed her.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'He changed her' means הגי gave אסתר vegetables, just as דניאל was given vegetables.

steps.title: What is 'oil of myrrh'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about six months with oil of myrrh and asks what this oil is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Six months with oil of myrrh.' What is 'oil of myrrh'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the מגילה and asks what 'oil of myrrh' means. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women brought to the king were prepared for six months with this oil. The term is unclear, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil of myrrh, a beauty oil used to prepare the women
What is? This asks for a definition.

phrases.english: "Six months with oil of myrrh."
What is "oil of myrrh"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the מגילה.

steps.title: Two definitions: perfumed oil or unripe olive oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says it is סטכת, a fragrant oil. רב הונא says it is oil from olives that have not yet reached a third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: it is סטכת. רב הונא said: it is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with two different definitions of 'oil of myrrh.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא identifies it as a known perfumed oil. רב הונא says it is a special oil pressed from very young, unripe olives.

keyTerms.meaning: That has not reached a third of its growth (very unripe)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: סְטָכַת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: setakt (a perfumed oil).
Rav Huna said:
Olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: סְטָכַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a perfumed oil called סטכת (רבי חייא בר אבא), or oil from unripe olives (רב הונא).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא and explains the oil's use
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה in a ברייתא also says the oil comes from olives less than a third grown, and explains that it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: אנפקינון is oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth. Why do they smear it on? Because it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב הונא's definition. It also explains why this oil was used on the women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses the same description as רב הונא, so רב הונא now has support from a תנא. The ברייתא adds a new detail: this oil was a beauty treatment that removed body hair and made the skin soft.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַנְפָּקִינוֹן — שֶׁמֶן זַיִת שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ,
phrases.english: Anpakinon is olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth.
And why do they smear it on?
Because it removes the hair
and softens the skin.

steps.whatToRemember: 'Oil of myrrh' is best explained as oil from unripe olives (רב הונא, backed by רבי יהודה). It was used to remove hair and soften the skin.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's definition from step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's definition of 'oil of myrrh' as oil from unripe olives.

steps.title: A hidden praise of אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'In the evening she went and in the morning she returned,' רבי יוחנן learns that אחשורוש did not have relations during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the evening she went, and in the morning she returned.' רבי יוחנן said: from the shame of that wicked man we learned his praise: he would not have relations during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains a פסוק that seems only to show אחשורוש's bad behavior. He points out that it also shows one good thing about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a new woman coming to the king every night, which is shameful. But since they came only in the evening, we learn that he kept a basic level of modesty and did not have relations by day.

phrases.english: "In the evening she went
and in the morning she returned."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
From the shame of that wicked man
phrases.notes: 'That wicked man' is אחשורוש. The shame is that he had a different woman every night.

phrases.english: we learned his praise:
that he would not have relations during the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִגְּנוּתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע לָמַדְנוּ שִׁבְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק shows that אחשורוש did not have relations during the day, which is a point in his favor.

steps.title: Everyone saw אסתר as one of their own people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains 'Esther found favor' to mean that each person thought she came from his own nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And Esther found favor in the eyes of all who saw her.' רבי אלעזר said: this teaches that to each and every person she looked like a member of his own nation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains why the פסוק says אסתר found favor with everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually people favor those from their own nation. רבי אלעזר says that everyone saw אסתר as one of their own, so everyone liked her. This also fits her keeping her true background hidden.

phrases.english: "And Esther found favor."
Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that to each and every one
she seemed to be from his own nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלְּכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נִדְמְתָה לוֹ כְּאוּמָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the next פסוק in the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר found favor with everyone because each person saw her as one of his own people.

steps.title: Why the month of טבת mattered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אסתר was taken to the king in טבת, a cold month when one body enjoys the warmth of another.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So אסתר was taken to King אחשורוש, to his royal house, in the tenth month, which is the month of טבת.' It is a month when one body enjoys being close to another body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק tells us the exact month אסתר was taken to the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבת is a cold winter month, when people enjoy the warmth of another person. That timing helped אסתר find favor with אחשורוש. The month is mentioned because it was part of the plan from Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth month, a cold winter month
One body enjoys another body (its warmth)

phrases.english: "So Esther was taken to King Achashverosh
into his royal house
in the tenth month, which is the month of Tevet."
A month in which one body enjoys another body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next פסוק, adding another reason אסתר found favor with the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was taken in טבת, a cold month when bodies enjoy each other's warmth, so the timing helped her win the king's favor.

steps.title: Why the king loved אסתר more than everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the double wording of the פסוק, 'more than all the women' and 'more than all the virgins.' It teaches that אסתר could seem like either one to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the king loved אסתר more than all the women, and she found favor more than all the virgins. רב said: If he wanted the experience of being with a virgin, he had it, and if he wanted the experience of being with a woman who was not a virgin, he had it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק, and רב explains why it compares אסתר both to 'women' and to 'virgins.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two different groups: 'women' (who were no longer virgins) and 'virgins.' רב learns from this that אסתר seemed to the king like the best of both groups. That is why he loved her above everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace and kindness, meaning she found favor
A virgin, an unmarried young woman
A woman who has already been with a man
He tasted, used here as a polite way of saying he experienced

phrases.english: "And the king loved Esther more than all the women
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 2:17.

phrases.aramaic: וַתִּשָּׂא חֵן וָחֶסֶד לְפָנָיו מִכׇּל הַבְּתוּלוֹת״,
phrases.english: and she found grace and favor before him more than all the virgins"
Rav said:
If he wanted to taste the taste of a virgin, he tasted it,
phrases.notes: 'Taste' is a polite way of talking about married closeness.

phrases.english: if he wanted the taste of a non-virgin, he tasted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בִּיקֵּשׁ לִטְעוֹם טַעַם בְּתוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the verse-by-verse reading of אסתר chapter 2. It moves from when אסתר was taken to the king (step 33) to how the king felt about her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double wording 'women' and 'virgins' teaches that אסתר seemed to the king like both a virgin and a non-virgin, so he loved her most.

steps.title: The king's feast, tax break, and gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the king's great feast as one of several attempts to get אסתר to reveal her identity. She did not reveal it after the feast, the tax break, or the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And the king made a great feast.' He made a feast, and she did not tell him. He lowered the taxes, and she did not tell him. He sent gifts, and she did not tell him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the king made the feast and the other gestures in the פסוק: he was trying to get אסתר to tell him where she came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists a feast, a 'release' for the provinces, and gifts. The גמרא reads all three as a plan to win אסתר over so she would reveal her people. Each time, the result is the same: she stays silent.

keyTerms.meaning: A tax, especially a head tax

phrases.english: "And the king made a great feast" (Esther 2:18).
He made a feast, but she did not reveal to him,
he lowered the tax, but she did not reveal to him,
he sent gifts, but she did not reveal to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and explains the king's actions as attempts to learn אסתר's identity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The feast, the tax break, and the gifts were all attempts to get אסתר to reveal her identity, and none of them worked.

steps.title: מרדכי's advice and אסתר's continued silence
steps.stepSummary: The king asks מרדכי for advice. מרדכי tells him to gather more women, because jealousy might make אסתר speak. Even so, she does not reveal her identity, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And when the virgins were gathered a second time.' The king went and took advice from מרדכי. מרדכי said: A woman is only jealous of another woman who competes with her. Even so, אסתר did not tell him, as it says: 'Esther had not told her family.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why maidens were gathered a second time: it was מרדכי's advice to make אסתר jealous so she would talk. The גמרא then shows from the next פסוק that this plan also failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king's earlier gestures were kind. This new plan tries jealousy instead: bring in rival women, and maybe אסתר will reveal herself to keep her place. The פסוק 'אין אסתר מגדת מולדתה' proves that she still stayed silent.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'her friend's thigh,' meaning a rival woman close to her husband

steps.confusionAlert: It is surprising that the advice comes from מרדכי, who told אסתר to keep quiet in the first place. The גמרא simply says the king asked him. מרדכי's advice did not actually force אסתר to reveal anything.

phrases.english: "And when the virgins were gathered a second time, etc."
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 2:19. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק: 'and מרדכי sat at the king's gate.'

phrases.english: He went and took advice from Mordechai,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the king, אחשורוש.

phrases.english: he said: A woman does not become jealous
phrases.notes: 'He' here is מרדכי giving his advice.

phrases.english: except of the thigh of her fellow woman,
and even so, she did not reveal to him,
as it is written: "Esther had not told her family, etc."
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 2:20. It is the very next פסוק, and it proves the plan didn't work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the king's attempts from step 35, adding a final attempt based on jealousy, and closes the unit with a פסוק showing they all failed.
steps.whatToRemember: The king tried kindness (a feast, a tax break, gifts) and then jealousy (more women), but אסתר never revealed her people, just as the פסוק says.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second gathering of maidens was מרדכי's plan to make אסתר jealous, but she still did not reveal her identity.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר opens a new verse explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר begins explaining the meaning of a פסוק. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is the meaning of what is written?
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רבי אלעזר is introducing a פסוק he is about to explain, and the explanation comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי דכתיב' is a standard way of opening a new teaching on a פסוק. It does not challenge anything said before; it just starts a new idea in the reading of the מגילה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written, a standard opening for explaining a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said,
What is the meaning of that which is written:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the unit about the king's attempts to learn אסתר's identity ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening line of a new explanation by רבי אלעזר; the content continues on the next amud.
